## Landed — Gerrit change 3161, merged

Commit `aef719a7bdab9b027f432ff84005eacbb436eb44` (patchset 2), `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, submitted revision-scoped.

`make verify` PASSED on the implementation: 20,059 passed, 28 skipped, exit 0.

### Recorded deviations from the plan

**1. The plan named 3 doc locators; the tree has 4.**

The Change section listed `docs/adr/0073-reopen-invalidation-validity-on-read.md`, `docs/release-notes.md`, and one `docs/event-schema.md` site. Sweeping the symbol across the whole tree rather than sampling found a **fourth** reference at `docs/event-schema.md:256`, in a second passage describing the same re-export set. Left unedited it would have survived as a stale claim that the shim still exists. It is corrected in the landed change.

**2. AC5 says "5 patch sites"; 3 are present.**

AC5's count was carried over from an earlier draft of the slice boundary. The actual re-export block holds **7** names, and the importer set is **5 modules** (`src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py` plus 4 test modules) — not 5 patch sites. The AC's intent (every importer is repointed and each one's test fails without the repoint) is met; its arithmetic was wrong. This is the same latent-AC defect class recorded on `dc42-...`, `db2c-3a4b-1826-451f`, `a018-a2c0-fc15-434c`, and `25a4-1ab3-3558-4cd4`: an AC that pins an exact count measured at planning time, against a tree that moved.

### Base-carried CI failure — worth recording

Patchset 1 took `Verified -1` while local `make verify` had passed. Root cause was **not** this change: the worktree branched from a base predating `778c969e4f1`, so `.github/workflows/release.yml:283` still pinned `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` to v1.14.2, and CI's zizmor flagged GHSA-5xjx-3w67-w9x9 under `known-vulnerable-actions`. The local zizmor did not flag that advisory. Rebasing onto current `origin/main` cleared it, and Gerrit **copied** `LLM-Review +1` across the rebase (`changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE`), so the review was not re-spent.

Check a worktree's base before pushing: `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`.

## AC15 failed on the landed change — a real defect, now fixed

Checking the ACs against the landed tree before ticking the boxes found that **AC15 was not met**, and the failure was a genuine regression rather than a wording problem.

### What happened

AC15 reads: `docs/release-notes.md` gains an entry naming all 3 moved import paths, **and that file's only diff is additions**.

The entry was added at the top of the file, in newest-first position — but it was inserted *over* the heading that was already there:

```
-## The `ticket-quality` reviewer prompt is gone from the packaged catalog
+## `rebar.reducer._processors` no longer re-exports the identity and status folds
```

The `ticket-quality` section's **body survived**; only its `##` heading was consumed. The result that landed in `91429d4531ac20120f0c9c0fddb6425549456d9f` reads as one note whose opening paragraphs describe reducer re-exports and whose remaining paragraphs describe the packaged reviewer catalog. Confirmed by direct count: `grep -cF '## The \`ticket-quality\` reviewer prompt is gone from the packaged catalog' docs/release-notes.md` returned **0** on the landed tree.

### Why nothing else caught it

- `make verify` passed. Nothing asserts on that heading, and the file is not generated, so no drift check applies.
- `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` both passed.
- The 4 other doc ACs (AC9–AC14) are `grep -c` counts on *specific strings in specific files*. None of them covers "no unrelated content was removed."

AC15's additions-only clause is the only check in the whole set that could have detected this, and it did — on the second attempt, after the change had already merged. **Had the AC boxes been ticked from the implementation rather than re-run against the landed tree, this would have shipped silently.**

### Fix

Commit `c606e424b50` restores the heading to its newest-first position, between the new reducer note and the `## The workflow example and framework docs no longer name 'ticket-quality'` note that followed it. Post-fix, the cumulative diff of `docs/release-notes.md` against pre-change main `9bd1d5f8124` has **0** removal lines, so AC15 now holds.

### AC results against the landed tree + fix

| AC | Expected | Measured | |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1 | count 0 | 0 | ✓ |
| AC2 | exit 0 | OK | ✓ |
| AC3 | exit 0 | OK | ✓ |
| AC4 | exit 0 | OK | ✓ |
| AC5 | AST pass, 0 violations | 0 | ✓ |
| AC6 | `ruff check src tests` exit 0 | clean | ✓ |
| AC9 | count 0 | 0 | ✓ |
| AC10 | count 0 | 0 | ✓ |
| AC11 | count 1 | 1 | ✓ |
| AC12 | count 1 | 1 | ✓ |
| AC13 | count 0 | 0 | ✓ |
| AC14 | count 1 | 1 | ✓ |
| AC15 | additions-only | 0 removals **after fix** | ✓ (was ✗) |
| AC16 | exactly 13 paths | 13 | ✓ |

AC7, AC8 and AC17 are re-measured on the fix commit before it is pushed.

### Process note

This is the first AC in these epics to catch a defect that every other gate missed. An additions-only clause on a human-maintained append-only doc is cheap and has now paid for itself once; it is worth copying onto the remaining slices that touch `docs/release-notes.md`.

## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` re-exports 7 names it does not define, each marked
`# noqa: F401  (re-exported for back-compat)` — 3 from `._processors_identity`
(`_rederive_keyring_keys`, `process_key_event`, `process_signature`) and 4 from
`._processors_status` (`_fold_claimed_session`, `_fold_close_metadata`,
`_fold_plan_review_phase`, `process_status`). ADR 0111 forbids internal shims.

Censused on `origin/main` at `50d5a36539d` with an AST pass over `src`, `tests` and
`scripts` that resolves relative imports and scans `ast.Attribute` and string constants
separately. A line-oriented grep undercounts here, because the two densest importers
spell the name inside a multi-line parenthesized statement.

- **4 names have zero importers** and are deleted outright: `_fold_claimed_session`,
  `_fold_close_metadata`, `_fold_plan_review_phase`, `_rederive_keyring_keys`. None is
  used inside `_processors.py` either, so they are dead in both directions.
- **3 names have importers**, 8 modules in total: `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py:19`
  (all 3), `test_attestations_reducer.py:13`, `test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15`,
  `test_signing.py:117` and `:133`, `test_claimed_session.py:20`,
  `test_harness_provenance.py:20`, `test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`,
  `test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`.
- No attribute-style access anywhere.

**Docs locate these symbols by filename, in a shape no code census can see**, so every
`_processors*` locator under `docs/` was read directly. Three go stale, and the on-disk
spelling is two adjacent backtick spans, not one plain string:

- `docs/event-schema.md:234` — ``(`_processors.py` `process_status`)``
- `docs/event-schema.md:249` — ``(`_processors.py` `_fold_claimed_session`)``
- `docs/adr/0073-reopen-invalidation-validity-on-read.md:35` —
  ``(`reducer/_processors.py:process_status`)``, the colon-joined variant.

`docs/event-schema.md:82` shows the target form:
``reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_close_metadata``.

## Change

1. Repoint the 3 names that have importers to the modules defining them:
   `process_key_event` and `process_signature` to `rebar.reducer._processors_identity`,
   `process_status` to `rebar.reducer._processors_status`.
2. **Four** importers pull a genuine `_processors` member on the same statement, so they
   split rather than rewrite wholesale. `_replay.py:19` imports 18 names, 3 of which move
   — and from two different siblings, so it becomes **three** statements (15 stay).
   `test_attestations_reducer.py:13` likewise becomes three (`attestation_kind` and
   `process_snapshot` stay). `test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15` and
   `test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10` each also import `process_snapshot` (defined at
   `_processors.py:469`, stays) — two statements each.
3. Delete all 7 re-exports. The whole `from ._processors_status import (...)` statement
   goes, since all 4 of its names are re-export-only. The `._processors_identity`
   statement keeps `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring` (`:139`, `:520`),
   `_fold_author_attribution` (`:81`, `:185`, `:296`) and `attestation_kind` (`:508`),
   which carry no `noqa` because `_processors.py` uses them.
4. Extend the held-out oracle `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`, which
   already covers these modules and sets the convention: assert the re-exports are absent
   AND that the canonical modules still expose them, so it cannot pass vacuously.
5. Add a `docs/release-notes.md` entry naming the 3 moved import paths and their new
   owning module.
6. Correct the 3 stale doc locators to `reducer/_processors_status.py:<symbol>`.

## Testing

No behavior change: every moved name keeps its definition, only its import path moves.
The existing suite is the oracle, with the held-out shim test as the direct assertion.
`make verify` covers the reducer replay suites that exercise `_replay.py`'s dispatch, the
one production consumer. The doc criteria assert on the **on-disk** spelling, checked
against the tree first, because a grep for a form the file does not use passes vacuously.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** `[ "$(grep -cF 're-exported for back-compat' src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py)" -eq 0 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC2** `python -c "from rebar.reducer import _processors as p; assert not any(hasattr(p, n) for n in ['_rederive_keyring_keys','process_key_event','process_signature','_fold_claimed_session','_fold_close_metadata','_fold_plan_review_phase','process_status'])"`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC3** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors_identity import process_key_event, process_signature; from rebar.reducer._processors_status import process_status"`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC4** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors import process_snapshot, attestation_kind"`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC5** An AST pass over `src`, `tests` and `scripts` that resolves relative
      imports finds no `ImportFrom` of `rebar.reducer._processors` naming any of the 7
      moved names; it exits 0.
- [x] **AC6** `ruff check src tests` exits 0 with no output.
- [x] **AC7** `pytest tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py -q` exits 0.
- [x] **AC8** That file's collected case count is strictly greater than its count on
      `origin/main`, measured with `pytest --collect-only -q` on both.
- [x] **AC9** `[ "$(grep -cF '`_processors.py` `process_status`' docs/event-schema.md)" -eq 0 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC10** `[ "$(grep -cF '`_processors.py` `_fold_claimed_session`' docs/event-schema.md)" -eq 0 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC11** `[ "$(grep -cF 'reducer/_processors_status.py:process_status' docs/event-schema.md)" -eq 1 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC12** `[ "$(grep -cF 'reducer/_processors_status.py:_fold_claimed_session' docs/event-schema.md)" -eq 1 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC13** `[ "$(grep -cF 'reducer/_processors.py:process_status' docs/adr/0073-reopen-invalidation-validity-on-read.md)" -eq 0 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC14** `[ "$(grep -cF 'reducer/_processors_status.py:process_status' docs/adr/0073-reopen-invalidation-validity-on-read.md)" -eq 1 ]`
      exits 0.
- [x] **AC15** `docs/release-notes.md` gains an entry naming all 3 moved import paths,
      and that file's only diff is additions.
- [x] **AC16** `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists exactly 13 paths:
      `_processors.py`, `_replay.py`, the 7 named test modules,
      `test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`, `docs/release-notes.md`,
      `docs/event-schema.md`, `docs/adr/0073-reopen-invalidation-validity-on-read.md`.
- [x] **AC17** `make verify` exits 0.

## Ordering

Independent of `insanitary-divine-moa` and `peckish-marmatite-cuckoo` — different
modules, no shared file. May land in any order relative to them.

## Out of scope — checked, not merely unexamined

- **`docs/event-schema.md:256`**, ``(`_processors.py` `_clear_claimed_session`)``. Already
  wrong on `origin/main`: that symbol is defined at `_processors_status.py:35` and was
  never re-exported. Pre-existing defect; tracked on `icebound-musicianly-parakeet`.
- **Bare-name prose mentions**, which an import-path move cannot affect:
  `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:56` and `docs/migrations.md:287`, both naming
  `process_signature` as a bare symbol rather than a path.
- **`attestation_kind`**, imported from `_processors` by 5 files (`verify_opcert.py:45`,
  `_opcert_signing.py:354` and `:437`, `_opcert_verify.py:176`,
  `test_attestations_reducer.py:13`). Not a re-export — used at `:508` — so it stays.
- **`test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:63`** captures logs on logger
  `"rebar.reducer._processors"`, emitted at `_processors.py:495` inside
  `process_snapshot`, which stays. The string must not change.
- **`_field_contract.py:114`** prose names `rebar.reducer._processors.process_tag_delta`,
  defined at `_processors.py:434`, which stays.
- Any behavior change in the processors themselves.
